extracted.intended_audience: emergency responders, employers, labor organizations, safety professionals, and other stakeholders interested in OSHA rulemaking and commenting on the Emergency Response NPRM
extracted.subtask_description: Summary and status page for OSHA's Emergency Response Notice of Proposed Rulemaking (NPRM) that explains the proposed replacement of 29 CFR 1910.156, the scope of worker protections, alignment with other federal and consensus standards, and the public input/hearing process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide basic workplace protections for emergency responders
rubrics_metrics.description: The focus of the Emergency Response proposed rule is to provide basic workplace protections for workers who respond to emergencies as part of their regularly assigned duties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intended outcome of the rule; establishes the general protective objective that the regulatory text and provisions should achieve.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expand scope of protected workers beyond firefighters
rubrics_metrics.description: The scope of protected workers under the proposed rule would be expanded beyond just firefighters to include workers who provide EMS and technical search and rescue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines who is covered: workers responding to emergencies as part of regularly assigned duties, explicitly including EMS and technical search-and-rescue personnel rather than limiting protection to firefighting activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cover a broad range of hazards encountered during emergency response activities
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed rule would expand the scope of the existing standard to include a broad range of hazards emergency responders encounter during emergency response activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulatory provisions should address the variety of hazards in dynamic and unpredictable response environments rather than focusing narrowly on firefighting-specific hazards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Align with FEMA emergency preparedness and response guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: It would also align the standard with FEMA’s emergency preparedness and response guidelines...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulatory language and program expectations should be consistent with FEMA guidance to promote interoperability and avoid conflicting requirements across federal guidance documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Align with NFPA standards on the safe conduct of emergency response activities
rubrics_metrics.description: ...and with NFPA standards on the safe conduct of emergency response activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorporate or be consistent with relevant NFPA consensus standards where appropriate, reflecting industry-accepted practices for safe emergency response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modernize and replace outdated Fire Brigades standard (29 CFR 1910.156)
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed rule would replace OSHA's existing Fire Brigades standard, 29 CFR 1910.156, which was originally promulgated in 1980, covers firefighting activities only, and has only had minor updates since it was published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criterion for rulemaking: update an old standard that no longer adequately addresses current response roles, hazards, PPE performance, and industry practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address changes in protective equipment performance and current industry practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Current OSHA emergency response and preparedness standards are outdated and do not address the full range of hazards... They lag behind changes in protective equipment performance and industry practices...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New requirements should reflect contemporary PPE capabilities and current industry operational practices rather than relying on legacy assumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure consistency with industry consensus standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Current OSHA emergency response and preparedness standards... are not consistent with industry consensus standards...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulatory provisions should be evaluated for consistency with consensus standards (e.g., NFPA) to reduce conflicts and leverage recognized technical expertise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solicit and consider robust public input including comments and hearings
rubrics_metrics.description: OSHA received more than 4,000 comments from public stakeholders and stakeholder organizations in response to the NPRM. In November-December 2024, OSHA hosted 11 days of informal public hearings where stakeholders and organization representatives provided testimony.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rulemaking process includes solicitation of written comments and holding hearings; the agency will review and evaluate comments and hearing transcripts to guide decisions. Effectiveness of the rule can be informed by stakeholder testimony and submitted data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain accessible docketed documentation for transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: Documents related to the RFI and NPRM are available in Docket # OSHA-2007-0073; documents related to the Emergency Response NACOSH subcommittee are available in Docket # OSHA-2015-0019. NACOSH documents related to the Emergency Response report are available in Docket # OSHA-2016-0001.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make relevant documents (NPRM, presentations, SBAR reports, NACOSH materials) available in public dockets so stakeholders can review supporting information and submit informed comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Differentiate rulemaking from technical assistance resources
rubrics_metrics.description: This rulemaking effort is separate from OSHA's technical assistance resources for emergency response and recovery workers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies that compliance requirements established by a rule are distinct from non-regulatory technical assistance; stakeholders should consult technical assistance resources for guidance but recognize they do not substitute for binding regulatory obligations.
